answer: Second-order arrival timing is the tell. Each new identity pays a small fee reclaimed only after a randomized delay, and the chain records the microsecond of every claim plus the signer's clock skew and first-packet route. A bot farm spawning a meadow of keys bursts them inside a tight window and reuses one outbound host, so their latencies stack into a narrow basalt column no honest crowd forms. Weight waits until a key shows a scatter matching organic drift; caps cluster like basalt shards from one vent, while real agents spread like tidewater across a lagoon.
